items.title: Section: The Eighth Power Opens — Recollecting Countless Past Lives Through Eight Sayings and Six Abbreviated Conducts

items.zh: 若於種種有情眾中，謂於東方南西北方，種種名字假設安立品類差別。隨先過去所有自體八言說句差別類中，隨念六種略所行行，有無量種宿住隨念。何等名為八言說句？謂如是名、如是生類、如是種性、如是飲食、如是領受苦樂差別、如是長壽、如是久住、如是所有壽量邊際。何等名為隨言說句六種略行？一者、呼召假名，二者、剎帝利等色類差別，三者、父母差別，四者、飲食方軌，五者、興盛衰損，六者、壽量差別。由諸世間依憑如是八言說句、六種略行，於自於他起言起說：此是我名，此是彼名。
items.en:
Eighth, the power of wisdom recollecting past abodes; first, stating [the point]. Among the various assemblies of beings, in east, south, west, and north, various names are provisionally established distinguishing different categories. Following each being's own past embodiments, in the categories distinguished by eight sayings, recollecting the six abbreviated conducts, there are countless kinds of recollection of past abodes.
Second, explaining; first, distinguishing characteristics individually; first, the manner of speech; first, the eight sayings; first, posing the question. What are the eight sayings?
Second, listing them. Such was one's name, such was the kind of birth, such was one's lineage, such was one's food, such was the distinct experience of suffering and happiness, such was one's long lifespan, such was the duration one dwelt, such was the very limit of one's lifespan.
Second, the six abbreviated conducts; first, posing the question. What are the six abbreviated conducts corresponding to these sayings?
Second, listing them. First, the provisional name by which one is addressed; second, the distinction of caste such as kṣatriya; third, the distinction of parents; fourth, the manner of food; fifth, flourishing or decline; sixth, the distinction of lifespan.
Second, explaining the distinctions individually; first, the provisional name of address. By relying on these eight sayings and six abbreviated conducts, worldly beings give rise to speech regarding themselves and others: "this is my name," "this is that person's name."

items.title: Section: The Eighth Power Closes — Caste, Parentage, Food, Fortune, and Lifespan Across Countless Recollected Lives

items.zh: 我是剎帝利，彼是剎帝利。我是婆羅門、吠舍、戍達羅，彼是婆羅門、吠舍、戍達羅。此是我母，此是彼母。如說其母，父亦如是。我食如是色類飲食、所謂酪、漿、羹、飯、糜等。彼食如是色類飲食，乃至廣說。我有如是色類興衰差別而轉，彼有如是色類興衰差別而轉。我住如是色類年齒，所謂或少、或中、或老。彼住如是色類年齒，乃至廣說。唯有爾所隨先過去所有自體八言說句差別類中六種略行，過此無有餘言說句及以略行。是故唯於如是品類發起隨念，更無有增。即於此中，若言說行所有行相，若言說句所有標說，及即於此隨起憶念，是故說言并相、并說皆能隨念。
items.en:
Second, caste distinction. "I am kṣatriya, that one is kṣatriya. I am brahmin, merchant, or śūdra; that one is brahmin, merchant, or śūdra."
Third, the distinction of parents. "This is my mother, that is that person's mother." As said of mothers, so too of fathers.
Fourth, the manner of food. "I eat such and such food — curds, gruel, soup, rice, congee. That one eats such and such food" — and so on at length.
Fifth, flourishing and decline. "I have such and such flourishing and decline as it unfolds; that one has such and such flourishing and decline as it unfolds."
Sixth, the distinction of lifespan. "I dwelt to such an age — whether young, middle, or old. That one dwelt to such an age" — and so on at length.
Third, the limit of recollection. Only these — following each being's own past embodiments, in the categories of the eight sayings, the six abbreviated conducts — beyond this there is no further saying or conduct. Therefore recollection arises only with respect to these categories, with nothing further added.
Second, concluding the essential meaning. In this very matter, whether through the characteristics belonging to these conducts, or through what is described by these sayings, and recollection arising accordingly — therefore it is said that both the characteristics and the description can be recollected.

items.title: Section: The Ninth Power Opens — The Divine Eye, Utterly Pure and Surpassing Every Human Sight

items.zh: 此中靜慮說名天住。眼依彼故，是彼果故，彼攝受故，名為天眼。是極圓滿、是善清淨靜慮果故，名極清淨。於其人中，所有名字皆不相似，是故說言超過於人。欲界天中亦有生得，名相似轉清淨天眼，人中亦無。
items.en:
Ninth, the power of wisdom regarding death and rebirth; first, presenting the faculty of sight; first, called the divine eye. Here, meditative absorption is called the divine abode. The eye depends on it, is its result, and is sustained by it; hence it is called the divine eye.
Second, called utterly pure. It is utterly perfect, wholesome, and pure, being the result of meditative absorption; hence it is called utterly pure.
Third, called surpassing the human; first, regarding what is cultivated. Among humans, there is no name resembling it at all; hence it is said to surpass the human.
Second, regarding what arises innately. Among the desire-realm heavens there is also an innately arisen version, called a resembling, pure divine eye; this too is absent among humans.

items.zh: 諸有情類臨欲終沒，名為死時；住在中有，名為生時。趣黑闇者，由

items.title: Section: Inferior and Excellent Signs at Death, and the Two Causes That Lead to the Lower Destinies

items.zh: 二種相，起如是類意生中有，如黑羺光及陰闇夜，故名惡色。趣明白者，由二種相，起如是類意生中有，如晴明夜及婆羅痆斯極鮮白衣，故名好色。諸惡色者，說名為劣；諸好色者，說名為妙。諸下劣者，名往惡趣；諸勝妙者，名往善趣。所有壞戒及彼等起，說名成就諸身語意三種惡行。有二邪見。謂壞見者所成邪見，誹謗一切；及住彼意異品類者所成邪見，誹謗賢聖。如是皆名謗賢聖者。由邪見故，計著邪因及以邪果；由此為緣，造作邪業。造邪業故，所有法受或現受樂，於當來世受苦異熟；或現受苦，於當來世受苦異熟。是故復說起諸邪見業法受因。彼雖成就其餘所有種種善法，而但由此往於惡趣，是故說言由此因緣。
items.en:
Second, the distinction between inferior and excellent signs. Every dark sign is called inferior; every bright sign is called excellent.
Third, the distinction between the lower and good destinies; first, generally indicating where one goes. Every inferior sign is called going to a lower destiny; every excellent sign is called going to a good destiny.
First, from broken precepts. Every broken precept together with the afflicted intentions arising from it is called completing the three kinds of unwholesome karma of body, speech, and mind.
Second, from broken view; first, stating the two kinds. There are two wrong views: the wrong view of one who has corrupted right view, denying everything; and the wrong view of one dwelling in a related but different position, denying the noble and the wise. Both are called denying the noble and the wise.
Second, showing how it arises. Because of wrong view, one clings to a false cause and a false effect; on this basis, one commits wrong karma. Having committed wrong karma, whatever is felt — whether presently pleasant, ripening painfully in the future, or presently painful, likewise ripening painfully in the future — therefore it is said that arousing wrong views is the cause of karma and its felt experience.
Second, concluding the cause and condition. Although one may have accomplished all manner of other wholesome deeds, one still goes to the lower destiny purely by this cause and condition; hence it is said, "by this cause and condition."

items.title: Section: The Four Elements Dissolve at Death, and Three Kinds of Dying Mind — Wholesome, Unwholesome, and Neutral

items.zh: 名色二種更互乖離，故名身壞。一切死中，如是死者最極下劣，故名極死。為欲開示那落迦想，是故說言墮險惡趣。為欲開示自性體事，是故復須說那落迦。由非法行、不平等行往趣於彼，故名為險。於此趣中，觸諸苦觸，長時種種猛利無間受諸苦惱平等出現，故名
items.en:
First, explaining the condition of coming to be born; first, called the breaking of the body. Name and form mutually separating from one another is called the breaking of the body.
Second, called the most extreme death. Among every kind of death, such a death is the most utterly inferior; hence it is called the most extreme death.
Commentary: as for "among every kind of death" — this means death with a wholesome mind, death with an unwholesome mind, and death with a neutral mind; together these are called every kind of death.

items.zh: 惡趣。墮下分故，大深坑故，難救拔故，甚可悲故，極下賤故，以大綺言常悲怨故，說名為墮。由能發起上品厭離，是故唯說墮那落迦。

items.title: Section: Hell's Torments Summarised, the Good Destinies Contrasted, and the Ninth Power Concludes

items.zh: 當知此中，若由此生、若得生已，受諸苦惱；若受苦已，復起所餘自業所作種種眾苦，如是一切由此諸想之所顯示。與上相違，隨其所應一切白品，皆當了知。此差別者，善行為先所有諸趣，名為善趣。受極樂故，名樂世界。
items.en:
Second, concluding the essential meaning. Know that in this matter — whether through the cause that produces such a rebirth, or through the suffering endured once reborn there, or through the further suffering arising from one's own karma even after the initial suffering has been endured — all of this is displayed by these various distinct names.
Second, the good destinies; first, showing the opposite case. Contrary to the above, every wholesome pattern, corresponding accordingly, should be understood.
Second, distinguishing the difference. The distinguishing feature is this: wholesome conduct coming first, whatever destination this leads to is called a good destiny; because one experiences supreme happiness there, it is called a world of bliss.

items.title: Section: The Tenth and Final Power — "My Birth Is Ended, the Holy Life Fulfilled" — and the Ten Powers Now Complete

items.zh: 一切諸漏所有隨眠無餘永斷，逮得能治勝無漏心、勝無漏慧，是其最勝增上心攝、增上慧攝。由漏盡故，說名無漏心、慧解脫。即此心、慧二種解脫，於最後有，說名內證第六神通，由依見道及依修道內所證故。既自證已，如實了知，隨其所欲能為他說，是故說言於現法中自證通慧，具足開覺，我生盡等諸句差別。廣說如後攝異門分，應知其相。
items.en:
Tenth, the power of wisdom regarding the exhaustion of outflows; first, presenting what is thereby overcome. When every latent tendency of every outflow is permanently severed without remainder, one attains the supreme undefiled mind and supreme undefiled wisdom capable of counteracting them, the very culmination of mastery over concentration and wisdom. Because the outflows are exhausted, this is called liberation of mind and liberation through wisdom, undefiled.
Second, explaining inward, personal realisation. This same twofold liberation of mind and wisdom, in one's final existence, is called the inward realisation of the sixth superknowledge, accomplished through what is personally realised by the path of seeing and the path of cultivation.
Third, genuinely awakening others; first, explaining. Having personally realised this, understanding it exactly as it truly is, one can teach it to others exactly as they wish; therefore it is said that, in this very life, having personally realised this understanding through direct wisdom, one is fully awakened, [declaring]: "my birth is ended" and the other such phrases, in their full distinctions.
Second, pointing [to the source]. This is explained at length in the Chapter Distinguishing Synonyms that follows; its characteristics should be known there.

blocks.text: The last three powers: remembering past lives, seeing beings die and be reborn, and knowing that one's own contaminants are exhausted. The passage on dying is one of the treatise's most detailed.
Venerable Miào Jìng: "after this body there is no other": the final existence.
Only these exist; beyond them there is no further saying or conduct. Master Cháng Bǎi: we always live in a world of names.

Absorption is the "divine abode"; the eye depends on it. Venerable Miào Jìng: one born with such an eye has only a resembling divine eye. (Untranslated, 0570b14: approaching death is called the time of death; abiding in the intermediate state is called the time of birth.)

subs.head: Two causes of the lower destinies

blocks.text: Master Cháng Bǎi: clinging only to emptiness, denying good and evil causation. Venerable Miào Jìng: cause and effect exist, and all dharmas are empty; the two do not conflict.

Venerable Miào Jìng: name and form no longer unite; one with good karma dies in relative ease, while one bound for the lower realms dies in pain. (Untranslated, 0570c08: why the fall to hell is called "falling": it is downwards, a deep pit, hard to escape, pitiable, utterly low; it is named to arouse strong revulsion.)
"My birth is ended, the holy life fulfilled." Master Cháng Bǎi: it is personally realised. Both lecture series continue into fascicle 50 without a break.
Seven grounds, ten perfections, thirty-two marks, ten powers. Behind the long lists is one idea: every quality of a buddha has a cause in practice.

quiz.q: Over what does recollection of past abodes arise, and why only this?
options: the six abbreviated conducts in the eight sayings; beyond them there is no other saying or conduct
quiz.why: Only these exist; beyond them there is no further saying or conduct. Venerable Miào Jìng says the same. Master Cháng Bǎi: we always live in a world of names.

quiz.q: Do the lectures agree on "the limit of lifespan" among the eight sayings?
options: they differ: Miào Jìng takes it as the final existence; Cháng Bǎi cites seven returns and also an age-based reading
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: after this body there is no other — the final existence. Master Cháng Bǎi: at most seven returns, and notes an age-based view.

quiz.q: Why is the divine eye called "divine"?
options: absorption is the divine abode; the eye depends on it, results from it, is sustained by it
quiz.why: Absorption is the divine abode; the eye depends on it. Venerable Miào Jìng: the eye is blessed by the power of absorption.

quiz.q: How does the innate divine eye of desire-realm gods compare with the cultivated one?
options: inborn, called a resembling pure divine eye, unable to surpass the eye of absorption
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: born with it, it's called a resembling pure divine eye. Master Cháng Bǎi: it cannot surpass the eye of absorption.

quiz.q: "The wrong view of one who corrupted right view, denying everything." How do the lectures describe it?
options: Cháng Bǎi: clinging to emptiness, denying karma; Miào Jìng: cause and effect exist while all is empty — the two don't conflict
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: clinging only to emptiness, denying good and evil causation. Venerable Miào Jìng: cause and effect exist, and all dharmas are empty; the two do not conflict.

quiz.q: "Name and form separate." How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain, and what of the dying moment?
options: name and form no longer unite; the wholesome die with some ease, those bound for lower realms in pain
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: name and form no longer unite; one with good karma dies in relative ease, while one bound for the lower realms dies in pain.

quiz.q: "In one's final existence, the sixth superknowledge." The English reading note says the available source ends here. What is the fact?
options: the lectures continue in fascicle 50 — only a fascicle break; Miào Jìng adds that the sixth power isn't gained at once
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: the sixth power isn't accomplished all at once. Master Cháng Bǎi: it is personally realised. Both lecture series continue into fascicle 50, so the note marks only a fascicle break.
